coder_source_notes: Survey reported 88% using generative AI for assessments (92% using any AI); speaker rounds to 90%.

coder_source_notes: The 2024 study (published 3 Sept 2025) states 95% of companies identified in 2024 are SMEs (2023 = 96%). The 96% is the prior-year figure. The AI sector study 2025 was published 29 Oct 2026, the day of the debate.

speaker: Kate Chaney

coder_source_notes: Lecture announced for Tuesday 18 October (2022). Speaker calls Russell a Stanford expert; he is at UC Berkeley. No transcript found.

speaker: Scott Arthur
quote: Even more concerning was the finding that little progress has been made in addressing eating disorder-related content on AI interfaces since a similar study was conducted in 2023—almost three years ago.
claim: CCDH found little progress in curbing eating-disorder content from AI chatbots since its 2023 study.
coder_source_name: AI and Eating Disorders: How generative AI is enabling users to generate harmful eating disorder content
coder_source_notes: Two sources: the 2023 baseline study (older, in main fields; PDF path dated 2023/08 seen in search results) and the 'recent' CCDH report (Fake Friend, Aug 2025, in other_sources).

speaker: James Frith
quote: However, the International Monetary Fund estimates that around 70% of UK workers are in exposed occupations. Around half of those exposed workers are in high complementary roles, where AI will enhance rather than replace their work.
claim: The IMF estimates around 70% of UK workers are in AI-exposed occupations, about half of them in high-complementarity roles.
coder_source_name: Gen-AI: Artificial Intelligence and the Future of Work (Staff Discussion Note SDN/2024/001)
coder_source_notes: The SDN says almost 70% of UK employment is in high-exposure occupations, roughly equally split between high and low complementarity. The figure is also repeated in DSIT's assessment of AI capabilities and the UK labour market; the speaker names the IMF, so the IMF note is dated. A separate IMF working paper (June 2024) gives 66.4%.

speaker: Zali Steggall
quote: Since August this year, the EU's AI framework has required certain deepfakes to be disclosed as artificially generated or manipulated. The framework also includes requirements concerning machine readable markings of some AI generated content.
claim: Since August 2026 the EU AI Act requires certain deepfakes to be disclosed as AI-generated and includes machine-readable marking requirements.
coder_source_name: EU Artificial Intelligence Act, Article 50 (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689)
coder_source_notes: Act published in the Official Journal July 2024; Article 50 applies from 2 August 2026. The 2026 Digital Omnibus deferred the machine-readable marking duty for systems already on the market to December 2026 but left deepfake disclosure in place (search results).

speaker: Baroness Harding of Winscombe
quote: The EU AI Act requires it without undue delay.
claim: The EU AI Act requires providers of frontier (systemic-risk) models to report serious incidents without undue delay.
coder_source_name: EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689)
coder_source_notes: Published in the Official Journal July 2024 (recall). Art. 55(1)(c) requires GPAI systemic-risk providers to report serious incidents 'without undue delay'.

coder_source_notes: Article 55 GPAI systemic-risk duties applied from Aug 2025. California SB 53 and New York RAISE Act not named by title.
